name: Evans Scholarship
value: Full four-year tuition and housing college scholarship for caddies.
deadline: Application, High School Evaluation, transcript, test scores and Caddie Evaluation expected complete by September 30; CSS Profile and FAFSA due October 15. The official pages list these as annual dates without a year.
apply: Apply through the Evans Scholars online application portal (opens August 1). Submit the High School Evaluation, transcript, test scores and a Caddie Evaluation, then the CSS Profile and FAFSA. Questions go to applications@wgaesf.org.
eligibility: Caddies who have caddied regularly and successfully for at least two years and continue caddying at their sponsoring club during the application year. Must have completed junior year with above a B average in college preparatory courses. Must show clear financial need and be outstanding in character, integrity and leadership. ACT or SAT scores strongly encouraged.
notes: The September 30 date is days away for seniors applying this fall. Financial need is a core requirement. Scholarships are used at the foundation's partner universities.

name: Hagan Scholarship
value: $1,000 initial award for college essentials, then up to $7,500 each semester for up to 8 consecutive semesters. Up to 1,500 scholarships for 2027-28.
deadline: Fall application available September 1, 2026, due December 1, 2026. Spring application available January 15, 2027, due March 15, 2027.
apply: Create a username and password on the online application portal and apply once (applicants may apply one time only). Submit a high school transcript and a letter of recommendation. Finalists provide a FAFSA Summary (US citizens) or citizenship documentation.
eligibility: Students in the high school graduating class at a US high school with an unweighted cumulative GPA of 3.50 or higher. Parents' adjusted gross household income for 2025 must not exceed $125,000. Must enroll at an eligible four-year college the first fall after graduation and apply for federal and state grants if eligible. Open to eligible students regardless of nationality or citizenship.
notes: Recipients must work 240 hours between January 1, 2027 and September 1, 2027 to receive the fall disbursement. Household income limit applies.

name: Daniels Scholarship Program
value: Up to full cost of attendance at partner schools; up to $25,000 per year at non-partner schools outside the four-state region; up to $7,500 per year at non-partner schools inside the region.
deadline: Application period September 1 to October 15, 2026, closing at 4:00 p.m. MT.
apply: Register and complete the online application on the Daniels Fund scholarship portal during the open period.
eligibility: Residents of Colorado, New Mexico, Utah or Wyoming. Unweighted GPA of 3.0 or higher. ACT of 18 or higher in each category, or SAT Math 490+ and Reading and Writing 490+. Family adjusted gross income of $100,000 or less, with allowances for additional dependents. US citizen or permanent resident.
notes: Income limit applies. Class of 2027 Daniels Scholars are announced later in the cycle.

name: Ford Scholars Program
value: Renewable award of up to $40,000 per year. The amount depends on financial need, college cost of attendance and other scholarships received.
deadline: Application available beginning December 1; complete by March 1, 2027.
apply: Submit the FAFSA (or equivalent), find and start the Ford Scholars application beginning December 1, and complete it by the March 1, 2027 deadline, following the steps on the foundation's scholarship page.
eligibility: High school seniors who are residents of Oregon or Siskiyou County, California, pursuing a bachelor's degree. There is no minimum GPA to apply.
notes: Award size is set by financial need.

name: Academic All-State Award
value: $1,500 award to each of 100 Oklahoma public high school seniors per year.
deadline: Applications open October 7, 2026 and close at 5 p.m. Tuesday, December 1, 2026.
apply: Create an account and apply on the foundation's portal. A school official uploads your transcript (PDF) and verifies eligibility. Name two non-family members to submit recommendation letters.
eligibility: Oklahoma public high school seniors who meet at least one threshold: ACT composite of 30 or higher, SAT (EBRW plus Math) of 1370 or higher, or National Merit Semifinalist. Applicants are evaluated on leadership, motivation, academic achievement and character.
notes: Public school seniors only. Honorees are recognized at the Academic Awards Celebration on May 8, 2027.

provider: Idaho Governor's Cup (Idaho State Board of Education)
name: Idaho Governor's Cup Scholarship (Academic)
value: Up to $5,000 per academic year, renewable for up to four years. A career-technical track pays $3,000 per year for up to three years.
deadline: Deadline for 2027-28 not yet posted. The state scholarship site says the application opens in early October.
apply: Complete the Idaho State Board of Education general scholarship application with a 500-word personal essay, documentation of volunteer work, community leadership and public service, and two letters of recommendation.
eligibility: Idaho residents graduating from an Idaho high school or Idaho home school with an unweighted cumulative GPA of at least 3.5, attending full time at an eligible Idaho college or university, with a strong commitment to public service.
notes: Confirm the 2027-28 deadline when the state posts it.

name: TILF Scholarships for UIL State Meet Competitors
value: About 300 new awards each year; more than $1.2 million funded across nearly 70 Texas colleges in 2025-26. Individual amounts vary by scholarship.
deadline: 2027 deadline not yet posted. The 2026 deadline was May 22, 2026.
apply: Submit the TILF application with a transcript listing SAT and/or ACT scores, a recommendation from a superintendent, principal, assistant principal, UIL coach or counselor, pages 1 and 2 of a parent's most recent IRS Form 1040, and your financial aid letter from your chosen college.
eligibility: Graduating seniors who competed at the UIL Academic State Meet, Congressional Debate State Meet, One-Act Play State Meet or Theatrical Design State Meet, or advanced to the octofinal round. Must plan to attend an accredited Texas college full time and keep a 2.5 college GPA (some awards require higher).
notes: Selection looks at consistent achievement in school and UIL competition, and takes a holistic view of financial need. Only UIL academic contest participation qualifies.

name: Triple 'A' Award (Academics, Arts, Athletics)
value: A four-year $1,000 scholarship for statewide winners in Class A and Class AA.
deadline: 2026-27 nomination form not yet posted (MSHSL posts it in October). Region deadlines are set by each administrative region committee.
apply: Nominated through your school's Activities Director. Each school can submit two finalists to its administrative region secretary by the region deadline.
eligibility: High school seniors with a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher at nomination who participate in at least one League-sponsored athletic program and one arts or activity program.
notes: School nomination required. Ask your Activities Director about your region's deadline.

provider: Lilly Endowment Inc. (with Independent Colleges of Indiana and county community foundations)
name: Lilly Endowment Community Scholarship
value: Full tuition, required fees and a book and equipment allowance for four years at an Indiana college. 147 scholarships statewide, awarded county by county.
deadline: Set by each county community foundation. Many class of 2027 county deadlines fell in late summer or early fall 2026 (for example, Tippecanoe County closed September 8, 2026).
apply: Apply through the community foundation in your home county. The county foundation nominates finalists and Independent Colleges of Indiana makes the final selection.
eligibility: Indiana residents graduating from an accredited Indiana high school by 2027 who plan full-time bachelor's study at an eligible Indiana college or university. Selection criteria, procedures and due dates vary by county (for example, one county weighs academic achievement, extracurricular and volunteer involvement and a personal essay).
notes: Check your county foundation right away; some counties have already closed for the class of 2027. Room, board and travel are not covered.

name: Mitchell Scholarship
value: $10,000 scholarship paid in four annual installments of $2,500. 200 awards statewide, at least one per Maine public high school.
deadline: Opens December 1, 2026. Due March 1, 2027 (college financial aid letter due April 1, 2027).
apply: Apply through the Common App or the Mitchell Scholarship Application (complete only one).
eligibility: Full-time Maine residents on track to graduate from a Maine public high school who plan to attend a two-year or four-year degree program at an accredited college. Selection is based on academics, community impact and financial need.
notes: Financial need is one of three selection factors.

name: Stephen Phillips Memorial Scholarship
value: Award amount not stated on the official criteria page.
deadline: 2027-28 dates not yet posted. The 2026-27 cycle had an Early Response deadline of noon April 2, 2026 and a regular deadline of noon May 1.
apply: Apply online through the fund's New Applicants page when the 2027-28 application opens.
eligibility: Permanent residents of Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Rhode Island or Vermont with a GPA of 3.0 or higher on a 4.0 scale and skilled writing. Must show unmet financial need of $7,000 or more at their chosen college and a Student Aid Index of 13,000 or less. US citizen, or noncitizen with current lawful presence and employment authorization. Must enroll full time in a first bachelor's degree.
notes: Strong financial need requirement alongside the GPA minimum. Watch for 2027-28 dates.

name: Rodeo scholarships for high school seniors (Metropolitan, Area Go Texan, Achievement and others)
value: $5,000 per year, renewable, up to $20,000 over four years. More than 800 scholarships awarded in 2026, including 350 Metropolitan awards.
deadline: Class of 2027 dates not yet posted. The most recent posted cycle opened December 1, 2025 and the online application closed February 2, 2026.
apply: One online application considers you for every Rodeo scholarship you qualify for. A school official or counselor completes a second portion.
eligibility: US citizens and Texas residents graduating from an eligible high school who complete the FAFSA and plan to attend an accredited, not-for-profit Texas university. Minimum SAT 950 or ACT 19 (Metropolitan also requires top half of class). Some categories are limited to certain counties or to 4-H, FFA, exhibitor or other groups.
notes: Evaluators award points for academics, leadership and financial need.

name: Civics Essay Contest
value: Most recent contest: $5,000 first place; $2,500 each for second and third place.
deadline: 2026-27 contest not yet posted. The 2025-26 deadline was February 6, 2026.
apply: Submit a 750 to 1,000 word essay on the posted constitutional topic (citing court cases) with the Contest Entry Form and Essay Release Form.
eligibility: Students in grades 11 and 12 (or equivalent) in New Hampshire.
notes: Topic and rules change each year; check back for the 2026-27 prompt.

provider: Oregon Office of Student Access and Completion (OSAC)
name: OSAC Scholarship Application
value: Many donor scholarships (more than 600) through one application; amounts vary.
deadline: 2027-28 dates not yet posted. The official page describes a November to March 1 application window with a February 15 Early Bird date.
apply: Create an OSAC account at oregonstudentaid.gov and complete one application to be considered for many scholarships.
eligibility: Oregon residents who are US citizens or eligible noncitizens, including graduating high school seniors. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.
notes: Early Bird awards are a drawing, not merit. Confirm dates when the 2027-28 application opens.

name: MaineCF scholarships
value: Many donor scholarships (40+ statewide funds plus regional funds); amounts vary.
deadline: Deadlines vary by fund. Most statewide funds list May 1; some list March 15 or April 15. The page does not state the year, so confirm for 2027.
apply: Apply through the MaineCF online application portal; a few funds use separate forms or select from existing applicants.
eligibility: Maine students. Awards consider academic performance, financial need, extracurricular involvement and work experience. Open regardless of citizenship status. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.

name: HCF Common Scholarship Application
value: Many donor scholarships (more than 300 funds); amounts vary. Average award in 2026-27 was $7,230.
deadline: Opens December 1, 2026. Closes February 1, 2027, 4 PM Hawaii Standard Time.
apply: Complete the HCF Common Scholarship Application in the HCF scholarship portal to be considered for all funds.
eligibility: Hawaii residents who demonstrate financial need and keep a minimum 2.0 GPA unless a fund states otherwise. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.
notes: Financial need is a general requirement.

name: Statewide Student Aid Program
value: Many donor scholarships; close to $8 million to nearly 2,000 students each year.
deadline: 2027-28 dates for four-year degree applicants not yet posted. The last posted four-year deadline was April 10, 2026.
apply: Apply through the ScholarshipSource portal with FAFSA information, essay responses and recommendation letters.
eligibility: New Hampshire students. Bachelor's-degree awards are based on financial need, academic merit and other non-academic factors. Citizenship is not considered in award decisions. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.

name: Rhode Island Foundation scholarships
value: Many donor scholarships; more than $4 million available in the 2026 cycle.
deadline: 2027 cycle not yet posted. The 2026 deadline was April 13.
apply: Apply through the Rhode Island Foundation online application portal at rifoundation.org.
eligibility: Rhode Island residents. Funds include general assistance and awards for specific majors and vocational training. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.

name: VSAC-Assisted Scholarships (Unified Scholarship Application)
value: Many donor scholarships (more than 150); amounts vary.
deadline: Opens October 1, 2026. Submit on or before February 10, 2027.
apply: Submit one Unified Scholarship Application to be considered for VSAC-assisted scholarships.
eligibility: Vermont residents unless a fund says otherwise; US citizens or eligible noncitizens. Some funds require financial need; others weigh academics, community service and other merit factors. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.

name: NCCF Universal Scholarships Application
value: Many donor scholarships; amounts vary.
deadline: 2027-28 dates not yet posted. The 2026-27 universal application ran December 16, 2025 to March 3, 2026.
apply: Create an account in the NCCF Scholarships Portal and complete the universal application. Some scholarships require separate applications.
eligibility: High school seniors and college students at nonprofit or public institutions; many funds are tied to North Carolina counties or schools. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.

name: CFMT scholarships
value: Many donor scholarships (more than 160 funds); amounts vary.
deadline: Current-cycle dates not posted on the scholarships page.
apply: One application through the CFMT scholarship portal.
eligibility: Students from Middle Tennessee. Funds support students from particular schools or areas, specific fields of study, students with significant financial need and other qualifications. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.

name: ICF scholarships
value: Many donor scholarships (more than 65 programs); amounts vary.
deadline: Applications open January 1 to March 15, 2027. Individual fund deadlines fall between February 1 and April 25.
apply: Select your Idaho region on the ICF students page and apply to each fund per its linked instructions (no single common application).
eligibility: Idaho students; many funds are limited to specific regions or counties, with GPA minimums typically 2.0 to 3.5. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.

name: WYCF scholarships
value: Many donor scholarships; amounts vary.
deadline: Current-cycle dates not yet posted. The page still shows the prior cycle (applications open October 1; last posted deadline March 3, 2025).
apply: Check eligibility in the scholarship table, then apply in the WYCF online system.
eligibility: Mostly Wyoming residents or graduates of specific Wyoming counties or high schools; GPA minimums range from 2.0 to 3.0 by fund. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.

name: ArCF scholarships
value: Many donor scholarships (dozens of funds); amounts vary.
deadline: Portal opens each year beginning February 1; deadline not posted.
apply: Create an account on the scholarship portal and complete the eligibility quiz to see matching funds.
eligibility: Mostly Arkansas students pursuing two- or four-year college, vocational or technical training. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.

name: ACF post-secondary scholarship application
value: Many donor scholarships (over 60); amounts vary.
deadline: Opens January 15 and closes March 15 (year not stated on the page).
apply: One login and one application in the ACF scholarship portal considers you for every scholarship you may be eligible for.
eligibility: Alaska students pursuing post-secondary education. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.

name: MCF scholarships
value: Many donor scholarships; nearly $1 million awarded for 2025-26. Awards generally $500 to $5,000, some renewable.
deadline: 2027 season dates not yet posted. The 2026 season opened January 1 and closed March 31, 2026.
apply: Take the eligibility quiz and apply through the MCF Scholarship Directory.
eligibility: Montana students. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.

name: SDCF scholarship portal
value: Many donor scholarships; amounts vary.
deadline: Portal opens September 15 and closes March 15 (year not stated on the page).
apply: Begin the application in the SDCF GOapply portal.
eligibility: South Dakota students. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.

name: DCF scholarships
value: Many donor scholarships; $1,001,500 to 237 students for 2025-26.
deadline: 2027-28 dates not yet posted.
apply: Apply through the DCF Scholarship Portal; review the DCF Scholarship Compendium for fund descriptions.
eligibility: Delaware students. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.

name: GKCCF scholarship portal
value: Many donor scholarships (hundreds); amounts vary.
deadline: Portal reopens for the 2027/2028 award year in December.
apply: Complete the general application at gkccf.academicworks.com, then apply to the matching opportunities it lists.
eligibility: Students in and around Kansas City. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.

name: CFSEM scholarship application
value: Many donor scholarships; amounts vary.
deadline: 2027 cycle not yet open. The 2026 cycle ran January 26 to March 16, 2026.
apply: Submit one application through the CFSEM portal with transcript, two recommendation letters, activity and employment information and essays.
eligibility: Students in Southeast Michigan. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.

name: CFM scholarships platform
value: Many donor scholarships; more than $170,000 in scholarship and award funds in 2026.
deadline: 2027 cycle not yet posted. The 2026 application ran January 15 to April 15, 2026.
apply: Submit one application and be matched with scholarships you qualify for.
eligibility: Mostly graduating high school seniors in Mississippi. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.

name: CFT universal scholarship application
value: Many donor scholarships; 415 recipients and $2 million awarded in FY25.
deadline: Universal application reopens in January 2027. 2026 fund deadlines ranged from February 13 to May 15.
apply: Apply through the CFT universal application portal; submit essays, two or more recommendations, FAFSA documentation and GPA verification as required.
eligibility: Mostly North Texas (Dallas, Collin, Denton, Tarrant, Ellis, Kaufman, Rockwall counties), with some statewide and national funds. GPA minimums range from 2.0 to 3.5. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.
notes: Most CFT funds combine financial need with merit.

name: ACF scholarships
value: Many donor scholarships; amounts vary.
deadline: Deadlines vary by fund. The page lists the 2026-27 school year application; confirm 2027-28 dates.
apply: Complete the eligibility questionnaire, then the high school application in the ACF portal.
eligibility: New Mexico residents. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.

provider: Washington Scholarship Coalition and Washington Student Achievement Council
name: theWashBoard.org
value: Many scholarships from Washington providers; free matching service; amounts vary.
deadline: Varies by scholarship.
apply: Create a free student profile on theWashBoard.org to be matched with scholarships and apply online.
eligibility: Washington students, whether attending college in state or out of state. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.

name: CFNN scholarship portal
value: Many donor scholarships (over 40 local funds); amounts vary.
deadline: Portal opened January 15, 2026; individual deadlines run from March 2026 through January 2027, so a few may still be open.
apply: Take the eligibility quiz and apply for matching scholarships within the portal.
eligibility: Mostly Northern Nevada residents; some funds are limited to Washoe, Churchill or other counties. Some awards are need-based and others recognize achievement. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.

name: OCCF scholarships
value: Many donor scholarships (hundreds of funds); amounts vary.
deadline: Dates not posted on the directory page.
apply: Apply through the OCCF scholarship portal (grantinterface.com).
eligibility: Mostly Oklahoma students, many from central Oklahoma. Some funds are faculty-nominated merit awards; others require financial need. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.

name: CFO scholarships
value: Many donor scholarships (over 100); amounts vary (for example, Tulsa Engineering Scholarship $24,000 at $3,000 per semester).
deadline: Dates not posted on the scholarship page.
apply: Apply through the CFO scholarship portal (one centralized application).
eligibility: Oklahoma residents or graduating seniors from specific Oklahoma high schools; GPA minimums typically 2.0 to 3.5. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.

name: Pittsburgh Foundation scholarships
value: Many donor scholarships; nearly $3 million a year from about 375 funds.
deadline: Applications reopen for the 2027-28 academic year in January 2027.
apply: Use the foundation's scholarship search tool; some funds route you to Scholarship America to create an account and apply.
eligibility: Mostly students in the Pittsburgh region. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.

name: CFWM scholarship application
value: Many donor scholarships (over 160 funds, over 1,000 awards, about $1.4 million a year). Students can receive up to $3,000 total.
deadline: 2027-28 dates not yet posted. The 2026-27 application ran January 1 to March 1, 2026.
apply: Submit one online application; the foundation matches you to every fund you qualify for. Include a recent transcript and FAFSA Submission Summary.
eligibility: Mostly residents of Franklin, Hampshire and Hampden Counties, with some funds for Berkshire County and Hartford County, Connecticut. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.
notes: Except for a few awards, financial need is strongly considered.

name: FFTC scholarships
value: Many donor scholarships (more than 150 funds); amounts vary.
deadline: 2027-2028 application cycle opens December 1, 2026 and runs to March 5, 2027.
apply: Search and apply through the FFTC scholarship portal (fftcscholarships.communityforce.com).
eligibility: Students in the Carolinas region, including high school seniors. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.

name: BGCF scholarship portal
value: Many donor scholarships (more than 50); amounts vary.
deadline: Opens December 15 each year. 2027 deadline not yet posted; the 2026 deadline was March 10, 2026.
apply: Apply through the Scholarship Portal to be matched with 25+ scholarships; a few funds use separate applications.
eligibility: Students in Central and Appalachian Kentucky. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.

name: BRAF scholarships
value: Many donor scholarships; from one-time $500 awards to four-year scholarships up to $20,000.
deadline: Dates not posted on the main scholarships page.
apply: Browse the BRAF scholarship directory and apply; some funds require the FAFSA first.
eligibility: Mostly Louisiana students. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.

name: Universal Scholarship Application
value: Many donor scholarships; the universal application covers more than 100, with hundreds more in the directory.
deadline: 2027 dates not yet posted. The 2026 universal application closed March 9, 2026.
apply: Complete the Universal Scholarship Application, and search the online directory for funds with separate applications.
eligibility: Mostly central Ohio students. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.

name: SVCF-managed scholarships
value: Many donor scholarships; close to 700 awards totaling more than $4.5 million a year.
deadline: 2027-28 dates not yet posted; the 2026-27 cycle is closed.
apply: Apply through the SVCF scholarship application; eligible funds appear in your application.
eligibility: Mostly California and Bay Area students (some funds for San Francisco or Santa Clara County, a few for other states). Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.
notes: Students are limited to one SVCF scholarship per year.

name: Universal scholarship application
value: Many donor scholarships (84 funds); more than $12 million awarded in 2025.
deadline: 2027 dates not yet posted. The last universal cycle ran December 15, 2025 to February 27, 2026.
apply: Apply for up to 25 scholarships with one universal application; other funds have separate applications and deadlines.
eligibility: Mostly Colorado students, including graduating seniors in the Denver metro area. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.

name: GRCF general scholarship application
value: Many donor scholarships (hundreds) through one application.
deadline: Dates not posted on the scholarships page.
apply: Complete the general application through the foundation's scholarships page.
eligibility: Students who have lived in West Michigan; some funds are for specific counties or groups. Individual funds have their own residency, school, major, merit and need rules.
